name: Ecuador
snapshot: Daniel Noboa took his war on gangs across the border, launching joint operations with the US and slapping punishing tariffs on Colombia.
culture: Ecuador spans Pacific beaches, Andean highlands, the Amazon and the Galápagos Islands, where Darwin observed finches. Quito's colonial centre was among the first UNESCO World Heritage sites. Kichwa communities keep strong Andean traditions, and the Panama hat is actually made in Ecuador, woven from toquilla straw.
society: Ecuador uses the US dollar and is the world's largest banana exporter. In a few years, drug gangs turned it from one of the region's safest countries into one of its most violent, with prisons run by cartels. Noboa declared an "internal armed conflict" in 2024. Indigenous movements have led powerful protests against fuel price rises.

story: Ten years ago Ecuador was one of South America's safer countries, wedged between the world's two biggest cocaine producers, Colombia and Peru, but largely spared their violence. Then its ports became the main exit for cocaine to Europe and the US, and the gangs followed. By 2025 it had the highest murder rate in Latin America, about 52 per 100,000, roughly one killing an hour (AFP via FMT). Daniel Noboa, a banana-fortune heir elected at 35, has answered with soldiers, prisons and a close alliance with Trump. In November 2025 voters rejected his plan to allow foreign military bases, a sharp personal rebuke.

In 2026 Noboa took the war across his border and into trade. In January he blamed Colombia's leftist president Gustavo Petro for failing to fight cocaine and illegal gold mining along the frontier, and slapped a 30 percent "security tariff" on Colombian goods; he raised it to 50 percent in March and 100 percent from 1 May (Al Jazeera). Petro called it a "monstrosity" that meant the end of the Andean trade pact for Colombia, and cut off cross-border electricity sales that Ecuador depends on during droughts. On 3 March Noboa and Trump launched a joint military operation in Ecuador against what the US calls designated terrorist organisations; Petro alleged bombs fell near farms on the border (Al Jazeera). The government says killings are finally falling: 14 percent fewer in the first quarter, 28 percent fewer in March, though 1,800 people had still been murdered by early April (El Diario). Critics say the war targets the poor while money launderers go untouched.
briefing.power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for four years with one re-election and can dissolve the unicameral National Assembly once, triggering new elections for both. Ecuador uses the US dollar as its currency.
briefing.holders: President Daniel Noboa (ADN), since November 2023, re-elected April 2025.
